simcc-simoc-2023-g1-01.title: Look at the last digit
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-01.body:
An even number ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. Only 1352 does.

**Answer: (C) 1352**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-03.title: Pair numbers that make round totals
Estimate to rule out choices
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-03.body:
The numbers are small to medium: eight numbers, the biggest 265, so the sum is a few hundred. Only 800 and 700 are close, and the last digits $6+5+7+6+4+3+5+4=40$ end in 0, so the sum ends in 0. Adding properly with pairs gives 800.

**Answer: (A) 800**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-05.title: Work backwards
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-05.body:
The last number is 5, and before that we divided by 8, so before that the number was $5\times8=40$. Before adding 12 it was $40-12=28$. Before multiplying by 4 it was $28\div4=7$. Before dividing by 5 it was $7\times5=35$.

**Answer: (D) 35**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-06.title: See the growth
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-06.body:
Each picture is a square grid of diamonds, with as many rows as the picture number. 9 rows of 9 give 81.

**Answer: (D) 81**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-07.title: Count layer by layer
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-07.body:
Count the cubes in each layer of the stack, from the floor up, and add the layers. The layer counts add up to 97 cubes.

**Answer: (B) 97**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-08.title: Count back, then forward
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-08.body:
Four days before Wednesday is Saturday (Tue, Mon, Sun, Sat). So the day before yesterday was Saturday, yesterday was Sunday, today is Monday, tomorrow is Tuesday, and the day after tomorrow is Wednesday.

**Answer: (C) Wednesday**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-09.title: Count the grid, then the corners
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-09.body:
The middle is a $4\times4$ grid. Squares inside it: 16 of size $1\times1$, 9 of size $2\times2$, 4 of size $3\times3$, and 1 of size $4\times4$. That is $16+9+4+1=30$.

Each of the 4 corner squares sticking out is one more square: $30+4=34$.

**Answer: (A) 34**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-10.title: Make the other three as small as possible
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-10.body:
The three smallest different even non-zero numbers are 2, 4 and 6. They add to 12. The largest number is then $40-12=28$ (which is even, as needed).

**Answer: (A) 28**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-11.title: Remainders
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-11.body:
The letters repeat every 5 columns: S, I, M, O, C. $62=12\times5+2$, so the 62nd letter is the 2nd letter, I.

The digits repeat every 4 columns: 2, 0, 2, 3. $62=15\times4+2$, so the 62nd digit is the 2nd digit, 0.

**Answer: (B) I, 0**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-12.title: List by first flower
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-12.body:
Number the flowers 1 to 7. Pairs with flower 1: 6 pairs. Then flower 2 with the later ones: 5 pairs. Then 4, 3, 2, 1. Total $6+5+4+3+2+1=21$.

**Answer: (D) 21**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-12.title: Multiply, then halve
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-12.body:
7 choices for the first flower and 6 for the second gives $42$, but each pair is counted twice (rose-lily and lily-rose). $42\div2=21$.

**Answer: (D) 21**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-13.title: Split into two lists
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-13.body:
Take every other number. 1st, 3rd, 5th, ...: $3, 7, 11, 15, 19$, going up by 4. 2nd, 4th, 6th, ...: $4, 10, 16, 22$, going up by 6.

The next number is the next in the second list: $22+6=28$.

**Answer: (B) 28**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-14.title: Find the rule
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-14.body:
Look at the first triangle: $9$, $7$ and $48$. Subtract 1 from the top and left numbers: $8\times6=48$. Second: $(5-1)\times(8-1)=4\times7=28$. Third: $(3-1)\times(6-1)=2\times5=10$. The rule: subtract 1 from the top number and the left number, then multiply.

Last triangle: $(7-1)\times(7-1)=36$.

**Answer: (C) 36**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-15.title: Place them in order
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-15.body:
Alex is ahead of David and Eric. David is ahead of Charlie, Eric is ahead of Ben, so Alex is first (nobody is ahead of him).

Eric and Ben have exactly one person between them, with Eric ahead. Eric can be 2nd (Ben 4th) or 3rd (Ben 5th, which is last, not allowed). So Eric is 2nd and Ben is 4th.

The remaining places are 3rd and 5th for David and Charlie, and David is ahead of Charlie. So David is 3rd.

**Answer: (D) David**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-16.title: One fruit at a time
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-16.body:
Two apples make 18, so an apple is 9. Then $9\times\text{peach}+\text{peach}=70$ means 10 peaches make 70, so a peach is 7. A pear is $18+7=25$.

**Answer: 25**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-17.title: Think of the worst luck
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-17.body:
There are 4 colours. In the worst case Emily takes one ball of each colour, 4 balls, and no two match. The 5th ball must match one of them.

**Answer: 5**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-18.title: Try numbers
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-18.body:
Multiples of 9: 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81, 90, 99. That is 10 two-digit numbers (9 itself is 1-digit). For 8: 16, 24, ..., 96 is 11 numbers; for 10: 10 to 90 is 9 numbers.

**Answer: 9**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-19.title: Largest and smallest
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-19.body:
Largest: start with 9 in the hundreds place, then make the tens digit as large as we can. The last digit must be even. $9+8+4=21$, giving 984 (9 in the tens place would need the last digit to be 3, which is odd). 

Smallest: the hundreds digit cannot be 3 (the other two digits would be 9 and 9, an odd last digit), so it is 4: $4+9+8=21$, with last digit even, giving 498.

Sum: $984+498=1482$.

**Answer: 1482**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-20.title: Count by the number of \$5 notes
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-20.body:
\$25 is odd, so we need an odd number of \$5 notes (\$2 and \$10 notes are even).

- One \$5: \$20 left. Use \$10 notes 0, 1 or 2 times and \$2 notes for the rest: 3 ways.
- Three \$5: \$10 left. One \$10 note, or five \$2 notes: 2 ways.
- Five \$5: \$0 left: 1 way.

Total $3+2+1=6$.

**Answer: 6**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-21.title: Last digit first
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-21.body:
The last digit must be 1 or 7.

Last digit 1: the hundreds digit can be 7 or 2 (not 0), then the tens digit is any of the 2 left over: $2\times2=4$ numbers.

Last digit 7: hundreds digit is 1 or 2, tens digit any of the 2 left: 4 numbers.

Total 8.

**Answer: 8**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-22.title: Look for the rule
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-22.body:
Write the two digits as a 2-digit number and compare. $3,6$: the number 63 and the answer 66. $2,7$: 72 and 75. $8,8$: 88 and 91. $5,1$: 15 and 18. The answer is always the reversed number plus 3.

For $6\blacksquare3$: reversed number 36, plus 3 gives 39.

**Answer: 39**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-23.title: Draw a bar
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-23.body:
Let the sister's gift be 1 unit. The brother's gift is 3 units, and it is half of all marbles, so the other half (3 units) is left after the brother. The sister takes 1 unit of that, leaving 2 units. 2 units are 18 marbles, so 1 unit is 9. At first he had $6\times9=54$ marbles.

**Answer: 54**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-24.title: Weight of one textbook
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-24.body:
Removing 2 textbooks takes away $2800-1900=900$ grams, so one textbook is 450 grams. 5 textbooks weigh $5\times450=2250$ grams. The empty backpack is $2800-2250=550$ grams.

**Answer: 550**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-25.title: Compare the two plans
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-25.body:
Giving 1 more bun to every student changes the situation from 3 buns spare to 6 buns short, a difference of $3+6=9$ buns. So there are 9 students. Buns: $6\times9+3=57$.

**Answer: 57**

simcc-simoc-2023-g1-25.title: Check
simcc-simoc-2023-g1-25.body:
7 buns each for 9 students needs 63 buns, and $63-57=6$ more. Yes.

**Answer: 57**
